# Discussion and conclusion {background-color="#491106ff"}

## Dialogue with the literature

:::: {.incremental style="font-size: 120%;"}

- Robust replication: higher meritocratic perceptions raise MJP [@castillo_perceptions_2025]
- Perceiving privilege lowers MJP; endorsing it raises it the most
- Embracing privilege means justifying more inequality and market welfare
- Speaks to welfare attitudes: brings market justice in, and meritocracy as legitimizer of inequality [@lindh_class_2020; @lindh_bringing_2023; @mau_inequality_2015; @castillo_perceptions_2025]

:::: 



## Methodological takeaways and implications

:::: {.incremental style="font-size: 120%;"}

- Broad measurement of meritocratic beliefs reveals distinct paths: perceptions vs preferences, merit vs privilege
- SEM tools (measurement error and latent paths) are a useful way to model them
- Transferable to other beliefs, criteria and domains shaping welfare attitudes
- Limits: cross-sectional and one country; next: conjoint experiments and cross-country analysis

::::
